page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled, featuring a 1229 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are present on this configuration.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1246.0 and a multi-core score of 7729.0, with a Passmark CPU score of 15944.59. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 830.88 GB/sec, which drops to 69.79 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 42.55 GB/sec. Database operations are supported by a Redis SET throughput of 13.8 million operations per second and a Passmark database score of 5436.86.

The E32-16ds_v4 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints relative to compute power. However, a notable tradeoff is its weak performance in processing prompts for medium-sized 7B LLM models, where it achieves only 24.46 tokens per second. It is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, Redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation.
